name: The Stone Pine of Citania de Briteiros

location.address: Acropolis of the Citania de Briteiros, EN 309 km 55, Briteiros Sao Salvador, Guimaraes

official_register.name: ICNF Arvores de Interesse Publico, AIP030880114I (Despacho n.o 12490/2021, 22 Dec 2021)

access: Paid entry to the archaeological site run by the Sociedade Martins Sarmento: 5 EUR (Visit Guimaraes; some guides quote lower, older prices), 2.5 EUR reduced, free for national residents on Sundays 10:00-12:30. Hours conflict between sources: Visit Guimaraes says summer (27 Mar to 31 Oct) daily 09:30-12:30 and 14:00-18:00, winter (from 1 Nov) Tuesday to Sunday 09:30-12:30 and 14:00-17:00 (last entry 16:30); the society's own page says Tuesday to Sunday 09:30-12:30 and 14:30-17:30. Closed 1 Jan, Easter Sunday, 25 Dec. Phone +351 253 415 969. Warning signs mark a safety perimeter under the crown (falling branches).
transport: About 15 km from Guimaraes centre. Guides give a 30 to 35 minute interurban bus from Guimaraes terminal plus a 10 to 15 minute walk from the stop; bus numbers disagree between sources (41/42, 163), and one older guide says no public transport. Check the operator before going.

location_site.name: Acropolis of the Citania de Briteiros

story:
The best evidence for this pine's age is a photograph taken by a man who died in 1899. Francisco Martins Sarmento, whose name the society that runs the Citania de Briteiros still carries, photographed the hilltop with the stone pine on it. In pictures Ilustracao Portugueza published in 1930, its crown is already broad and rounded. Guimaraes' cultural landscape atlas reads those images as making it more than 120 years old, and Portugal's forest service put it at 130 in 2020.

It stands on the acropolis of the hillfort and can be picked out from a long way off, marking Monte de Sao Romao. That is one reason the municipality asked in 2018 for it to be protected, and the state classified it as a tree of public interest in December 2021. A single trunk 3.6 metres round carries a wide, open crown on big spreading limbs. The forest service record gives a height of 25 metres and a crown 26.5 metres across. The decree that protects it gives 20 and 23. Both figures are official, so take the range.

Its age is starting to tell. A 2020 university assessment advised against pruning, and only two dry lower limbs came off. Signs now mark a perimeter under the crown because branches fall.

Entry is 5 euros, and the official sources disagree on opening hours, so check first. Briteiros is 15 kilometres from Guimaraes, and guides disagree on which bus gets you there.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the single trunk, 3.6 metres round, under a wide, open crown on big spreading limbs. It stands on the acropolis of the Citania de Briteiros, inside a ring of warning signs.

name: The Camellia of Casa de Margaride
age_estimate: over a century, possibly around 300 years

location.address: Casa de Margaride / Villa Margaridi, Avenida Rio de Janeiro, Margaride, Mesao Frio, Guimaraes

official_register.name: ICNF Arvores de Interesse Publico, Casa de Margaride rows (Despacho n.o 837/2022)

access: Private estate, garden open as paid entry by appointment: the Associacao Portuguesa dos Jardins Historicos lists it as 'Paid entry / Access by appointment' (contact on its page: casademaride@gmail.com, +351 932 671 231). Owner-led visits; an older press piece (evasoes.pt, c. 2022, seen only as a search summary, page blocked) gave 8 EUR per person with a tasting of the estate's wine, so confirm the price. No standing opening hours published. Garden joined the European Route of Historic Gardens in October 2026; the owner expects about 2,000 visitors in 2026. Not visible from the road.

location_site.name: Front courtyard (terreiro) of Casa de Margaride

verify_notes: Settles the access question left open by earlier passes (2026-08-16, 2026-11-13): hard rule 10 counts paid entry and bookable tours as yes, and the Portuguese Historic Gardens Association's inventory entry states paid entry by appointment with a contact. Facts below seen on fetched pages. WILDER (2024): 2024 Portuguese Tree of the Year, 3,900 votes, ahead of the Sobreiro do Rei (3,075); Camellia japonica with bell-shaped crown, 6.30 m crown diameter and 6.15 m height, classified of public interest by Despacho 837/2022; 'estimated about 300 years'; stands in the front courtyard (terreiro) of the house; camellias came via the sailors of the Discoveries. GUIMARAES AGORA 2026-10-13: same specimen was Tree of the Year of Guimaraes 2023, of Portugal 2024, and in 2025 represented Portugal in European Tree of the Year, 4th place (alive 2025-26); garden classified 2022 as Arvoredo de Interesse Publico, three trees classified individually that year; house and garden Monument of Public Interest 2012; baroque garden c. 1675, same family 13 generations, documented from 1021; walled, three sequential spaces. Separate feature: the Casa de Fresco, a camellia about 15 m tall inside a box hedge circle about 40 m round (labpaisagem: about 39 m, two Camellia japonica, cultivar 'Pompone' forming almost all of it); it is not the Tree of the Year camellia, do not merge them. DISPUTES: age 'about 300 years' (Wilder) versus 'over 100 years' (Jornal de Noticias via a search summary, and the decree wording quoted by labpaisagem); ICNF rows for the estate give 130 years at last measurement (cameleira girth 1.4 m at 41.45046,-8.27680; garden conjunto; pereira girth 1.9 m; diospireiro girth 1.6 m; all 130y). Age kept broad 100 to 300. girth_cm left out: the register 1.4 m is not shown to be this trunk. PIN: ICNF coordinate, not shown to land on this crown, so approximate; the small site is the front courtyard. Alive: dated 2025 contest and 2026 news; lifecheck not run. Photo not checked (not this pass's job). The pereira and diospireiro rows (130y) stand within about 50 m of the same coordinate and are not separate collectible points.
